text:
Zoe: Heads-up 3: we need a compact battlecard + two bench narratives for next week's launch email and the webinar. Keep it < 1 pager for SDRs.

Marco: Goal: three defenders we can use in 30s pitches. My draft verbs: 'Serve confidently', 'Unify deployments', 'Guarantee availability under strain'.

Lina: Tone note: don't lead with raw throughput numbers. Use comparative language: 'consistent p95 latency in production workloads' and 'engineered batching that reduces per-token tail cost'.

Casey: For the bench narratives I want two arcs: one for chat-heavy SaaS (steady token rates) and one for bursty ingestion (variable seq len). Each should list workload, test harness, and topline outcome (no hard numbers on hero).

Zoe: Good. Also include a short slide on fallbacks/rollouts. SDRs love a one-line demo script: "If latency spikes, fallback to a compatible hosted variant and notify the user with degraded-mode messaging."

Marco: Suggested hero soundbites (30s each):
- Dev-first: "Same API. Same tools. Run where you need it."
- Econ-first: "Predictable unit costs via workload-aware batching and KV caching."
- Trust-first: "Private deployments, KMS integration, and audit trails for regulated apps."

Lina: Email subject A/B ideas:
- A: "Cut inference surprises: predictable latency, predictable costs"
- B: "Ship LLM features without firefighting"
- C: "Run models where your data and SLAs need them"

Casey: Intercom routing plan: tag = {demo, enterprise-dedicated, technical-eval}. Workflow: enterprise-dedicated -> auto-assign to solutions-eng + high-touch SDR; demo -> schedule product demo; technical-eval -> send bench notebook + invite to private slack.

Zoe: SDR op snippets to include in one-pager: 3 objections + 1-liner rebuttals. Example:
- "We already have endpoints": "Redwood unifies those endpoints under a single runtime + transparent cost/latency dashboards."
- "We can't risk cold starts": "Our prewarmed pools + KV cache keep tail latency predictable."

Marco: Micro-code example for routing fallback to paste into the playbook:
```
# fallback example (pseudo)
policy = get_routing_policy(customer="acme")
if policy.capacity.reserved < policy.threshold:
  forward(req, model_variant="fallback-compatible", tags=["degraded-mode"]) 
  emit_metric("fallback.trigger", 1)
else:
  forward(req, model_variant="primary-reserved")
```

Lina: Webinar skeleton: 1) 5m intro & positioning, 2) 8m bench methodology, 3) 10m live demo (canary + rollback + routing), 4) 15m panel Q&A (compliance + ops), 5) 2m CTA. Keep the demo scripted with a predictable failure to show fallback.

Casey: Logistics: landing page is live (ops-bot). We need slides + one-pager for SDRs by Tue noon; bench narrative drafts by Wed; final battlecard + Intercom flows by Fri.

ops-bot: Landing page created -> /events/serve-first-ops. Recording room reserved Thu 10:30 PT.

Zoe: Assignments: Marco -> battlecard & bench narratives; Lina -> email copy + webinar poll; Casey -> Intercom routing + SDR one-pager. I'll stitch + proof and post to #marketing-final on Friday AM.

Marco: I'll also add 2 quick GIFs showing canary rollback for the deck.

Lina: I'll draft the poll: "Which is your priority? Latency | Cost | Control" and add a slide with expected audience outcomes.

Casey: Will set the Intercom tags and create the automation rules. Will share a screenshot of the flow here when done.

Zoe: Great work team. Keep responses short in the doc; SDRs hate long pages. :sparkles:
